# Embassy v1.5.0

The release where the gateway survives the world changing around it. v1.4.0 shipped and was unrunnable within minutes — Claude Code auto-updated one patch version and an exact-string gate refused to start the broker. v1.4.1 moved the pin; v1.5.0 removes the disease.

**Compatibility is evidence, never a version string**

- Provider admission follows one ladder. A certified build is writable. A same-major build whose bounded live probes all pass is writable when those probes cover the write path — true for Claude, whose writes fail loudly per operation; an untested Codex build stays monitor-only, because read probes never earn `turn/start` authority. Failed probes or a different major quarantine *that provider alone*, write-fenced and loudly diagnosed, while the broker, control socket, dashboards, and the other provider keep running. Nothing version-shaped can stop the broker from starting anymore — that refusal is reserved for lease conflicts, corrupt state, and OS-boundary attestation failures, the things that make running actually unsafe.
- Persisted compatibility evidence is validated against its own internal consistency, never against the current build's lists — a row recorded today loads under every future release, in both directions. The same law now governs all persisted history: what a past broker legitimately wrote is not invalidated by today's configuration.
- The registry reader is strict about every field it uses and tolerant of fields it doesn't know, so a Claude Code update that adds a field can no longer make your sessions invisible. Rejected records are counted and shown instead of silently dropped.

**The watch diet**

- The progress watch keeps all six of its promises with roughly a third of the machinery. Its journal speaks three words — opened, replaced, settled — each with who and why. Migration from v1.4 settles every live watch exactly once, journaled, and loads regardless of today's capacity knobs.
- Watch supervision is quieter and truer: replacement requires the incumbent owner, attribution cannot be forged, and a settled watch cannot be resurrected.

**Embassy says what it knows**

- A steering message tells its recipient how many earlier messages are queued ahead of it — a steer can no longer invisibly reference mail that hasn't arrived.
- A stalled queue names the actual dynamic and the remedy: queued mail reaches a busy recipient when its turn ends; end the turn if you control it.

**One vocabulary, two honest dashboards**

- The static and live dashboards now render one shared semantic layer and can no longer disagree about what a state means. A monitor-only route renders as needing attention — never as a ready exchange. A quarantined provider owns its recovery guidance instead of being decorated with suggestions that cannot cure it. The static view cannot materialize message bodies at all, by construction.

**Less churn, fewer lies**

- Claude routes no longer cycle through stale/reobservation on every broker restart or upgrade — the endpoint generation is a constant, because nothing varies underneath it.
- Every user-facing sentence was checked against the code: the dashboard no longer warns that restarts abandon queued mail (they never did, since v1.2), the privacy footnote says which rows show bodies, and an oversized message is told the cap and the remedy.

**The repo now documents how it is built — and what it refuses to build**

- `docs/DECLINED.md` records what we considered and chose not to build, with reasons. AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md carry the two-axis ticket system (effort budgets × blast-radius ratings) this release was engineered under, by two AI engineers working priced, windowed tickets in one tree.

**Compatibility pins** — Claude Code 2.1.227 tested (any 2.x with passing probes runs; peer protocol 1), Codex App Server 0.147.0 certified for writes, Node.js ≥ 20, macOS only.

Upgrading from v1.4.x needs nothing: state loads cleanly, live watches settle once with a journaled record, and Claude routes re-anchor themselves a single final time.

Unofficial community project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or OpenAI.
